definitions.title: Direct Comparison Test (DCT)
definitions.latex: 0 \le a_n \le b_n: \quad \sum b_n < \infty \implies \sum a_n < \infty; \quad \sum a_n = \infty \implies \sum b_n = \infty
definitions.statement: If terms of a non-negative series are term-by-term bounded by a convergent series, the smaller series converges. If bounded below by a divergent series, the larger series diverges.
definitions.explanation: Compares unknown series against known p-series or geometric benchmarks.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Smaller than convergent is convergent; larger than divergent is divergent.

definitions.title: Limit Comparison Test (LCT)
definitions.latex: \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{a_n}{b_n} = L \in (0, \infty) \implies \sum a_n \text{ and } \sum b_n \text{ share the same fate}
definitions.statement: If the limit of the ratio of terms a_n/b_n is a finite positive number L, then both series either converge together or diverge together.
definitions.explanation: Eliminates delicate inequality checking by focusing on asymptotic leading behavior.
definitions.keyTakeaway: If terms behave proportionally for large n, their series share convergence behavior.
